themes.resolution: Inline head script reads localStorage 'dl-theme' (system | light | dark) and sets data-theme before first paint; colorMeta.<token>.dark holds the dark value.

display.purpose: The single headline number of a result (route travel time).

title.purpose: Section headings; panel heads use title-sm.

label.purpose: Field labels, table headers, badges, legends. Sentence case.

data.purpose: Hashes, coordinates, clock, timestamps, strip stats, kbd, commands only (11–13px).

shadows.name: shadow-sm
shadows.purpose: Hairline lift: panels, map tools, map hint, active segment.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The single ease-out curve for every transition.

motion.name: duration-state
motion.purpose: Hover, press, segment and input state changes (table rows 120ms).

motion.name: duration-overlay
motion.purpose: Toast rise (8px) and scrim fade; mobile drawer slides at 220ms.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: Entrance by position only, from an already-visible default.

motion.name: search-sweep
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: four small multiples reveal settled nodes together.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: CSS animation/transition durations collapse to 1ms; the search sweep jumps to its final state

narrative.overview:
DispatchLab is a developer-platform console, played straight in the register of Vercel, Cloudflare and Linear dashboards. The road map is a precise instrument set inside a calm product shell. It is not a logistics control room: the shell is neutral grey, structured by hairline borders and quiet radii, and colour is spent only where it carries meaning. That means the route, the four algorithms, the dispatch policies, courier states, and pass, warn or fail status.

Density is operational. Body text is 14px, controls are 32px tall, and every number is set in tabular figures. Each view is either a scrolling page of panels (max 1240px) or a full-bleed workspace where the map fills the stage and a fixed inspector holds the controls and results. Light and dark themes are complete token sets. The theme is resolved from `localStorage` or the system preference before first paint, so the page never flashes the wrong theme.

Motion stays out of the way. State changes take 150 to 250ms with a single ease-out curve. The one authored moment is the search sweep, when four small-multiple maps reveal each algorithm's settled nodes in settle order.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral greys, hairline borders, one orange accent, and complete light and dark themes.
Geist Sans for the interface and Geist Mono for data only, both self-hosted.
Inverted solid primary buttons. Segmented controls instead of tabs or toggles.
A workspace layout: map stage plus a 372px inspector.
The four-map search strip as the signature element.
Colour as meaning, never decoration. Status is always paired with an icon or a word.

rules.name: The Reserved Series Rule
rules.body: The four algorithm hues belong to the algorithms and nothing else. Policies, courier states, status and chrome never borrow them, and a new algorithm view reuses the same four hues.

rules.name: The One Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only brand hue. It marks the route and the things a route connects (destination, restaurant), plus the Greedy ETA policy. Never use it for decoration, section fills or headings.

rules.name: The Paired Status Rule
rules.body: Status colour never stands alone. Every ok, warn or err fill carries an icon or a word, such as "4 of 4 agree on cost" with a check.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono sets machine output only: hashes, coordinates, timestamps, commands and per-algorithm stats. Interface copy, headings and labels are always Geist Sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change or be compared uses tabular figures. That covers table cells, facts, inputs, bars and the big result number.

rules.name: The Border First Rule
rules.body: Depth is drawn with 1px borders and tone steps. If an element needs a shadow to be told apart from its neighbour, fix its border or its tone instead.

rules.name: The Visible Default Rule
rules.body: Entrances never start from opacity 0. Content is visible at rest and only settles into position.

rules.name: The One Sweep Rule
rules.body: The search sweep is the only authored animation. Every other motion is a 150–250ms ease-out state change.

dos: Do make the primary action an inverted solid button (ink on light, near-white on dark), with one per context.
Do use the segmented control (sunken track, raised active segment) for every choice among two to five modes.
Do keep the four algorithm hues for the algorithms only, and colour policies grey (Nearest) and orange (Greedy ETA).
Do set hashes, coordinates, timestamps and commands in Geist Mono, and every comparable number in tabular figures.
Do build map views as a workspace: the map stage plus a 372px inspector, with floating surface chips over the canvas.
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines and tone steps, using 6px radii for controls and 12px for panels.
Do define every new colour for both themes on `:root` and `[data-theme="dark"]`.
Do keep state transitions to 150–250ms on the single ease-out curve.
donts: Don't build a logistics "control room": no dark neon maps, glowing routes or gauge cards.
Don't reuse an algorithm series hue for a policy, a courier state, a status or chrome.
Don't use orange for decoration, headings or section fills.
Don't use Geist Mono for interface copy, headings or labels.
Don't fade entrances in from opacity 0, and don't add authored animation beyond the search sweep.
Don't rely on colour alone for status. Pair it with an icon or a word.
Don't load fonts, tiles or scripts from external hosts. Everything is self-hosted and must open from `file://`.
